definitions.explanation: The ability to perceive odors through the nose. One of the five senses.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}は{嗅覚|きゅうかく}が{非常|ひじょう}に{発達|はったつ}している。
examples.english: Dogs have a highly developed sense of smell.

examples.japanese: {風邪|かぜ}をひいて{嗅覚|きゅうかく}が{鈍|にぶ}くなった。
examples.english: I caught a cold and my sense of smell became dull.

examples.japanese: {嗅覚|きゅうかく}で{食|た}べ{物|もの}の{新鮮|しんせん}さが{分|わ}かる。
examples.english: You can tell the freshness of food by smell.

notes:
{嗅覚|きゅうかく} refers to the sense of smell.

The five senses ({五感|ごかん}):
- {視覚|しかく} (sight)
- {聴覚|ちょうかく} (hearing)
- {嗅覚|きゅうかく} (smell)
- {味覚|みかく} (taste)
- {触覚|しょっかく} (touch)

Common expressions:
- {嗅覚|きゅうかく}が{鋭|するど}い (to have a keen sense of smell)
- {嗅覚|きゅうかく}が{鈍|にぶ}い (to have a dull sense of smell)
- {嗅覚|きゅうかく}{障害|しょうがい} (olfactory dysfunction)
- {嗅覚|きゅうかく}を{失|うしな}う (to lose one's sense of smell)

Note:
Loss of {嗅覚|きゅうかく} was recognized as a COVID-19 symptom and brought attention to this often-overlooked sense. The Japanese word for smell as a noun is {匂|にお}い/{臭|にお}い, while {嗅覚|きゅうかく} refers specifically to the sensory ability.
